name: BTR-82A

placement_rationale.text: BTR-82A adds a 30mm autocannon over the older BTR-80 but remains a thinly armored wheeled troop carrier, not a tank-class direct-fire asset, so 7 km in the near-operational band is consistent with its road-mobility role rather than a close ambush posture. That places it inside the ~30 km drone-dense corridor doctrine.md documents either side of the front, matching the asset's own contrast_vs_traditional note that wheeled rear movement is no longer the relatively safe route it once was.

cost.display: No clean current unit price; 5,000+ units produced historically

key_facts.label: Main armament
key_facts.value: 2A72 30mm autocannon (upgraded from BTR-80's machine-gun-only armament), 8x8 wheeled, amphibious

characteristics: 2A72 30mm autocannon (upgraded from BTR-80's machine-gun-only armament), 8x8 wheeled, amphibious
Strength: Autocannon upgrade over the older BTR-80 gives real direct-fire capability rather than just troop transport
Limitation: Wheeled platform less capable off-road than tracked IFVs; thin armor typical of the BTR family
Estimated quantity available: Widely fielded; exact current total not fully disclosed
employment_notes: Represents the modernization pathway Russia used to upgrade its large legacy BTR-80 fleet incrementally rather than replace it outright
contrast_vs_traditional: Wheeled APC doctrine like the BTR-82A's traded protection for road-speed troop transport behind the line. That tradeoff assumed the route itself was relatively safe once past the immediate front — an assumption the drone-dense corridor doctrine.md documents running roughly 30 km either side of the line has quietly erased for wheeled movement well behind what used to count as the forward edge.
